A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 17-page versions of BNMusic. Their main text, equations, Tables 1–3, Figures 1–8 and Appendices A–C support reliable comparison through text extraction and rendered-page inspection.

before.justification: V2 reports original objective evaluations, human-listening results and component ablations in Tables 1–3, plus a loudness–FAD experiment in Appendix A.

after.justification: V3 retains these original empirical results, including the objective comparisons, subjective scores, ablations and appendix loudness analysis.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix B retain the same frozen Riffusion-based outpainting/inpainting procedure, adaptive-amplification objective and audio reconstruction process.

E1.justification: Both versions use EPIC-SOUNDS and ESC-50 environmental noise, MusicBench music and prompts spanning the same seven genres. No datasets, tasks or noise scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain Random Music, melody-conditioned MusicGen and Riffusion A2A, with Noise Only also included in Table 1. The removed DiffSound citation was not an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Section 4 retains identical sample counts, reference-data allocation, loudness normalization, FAD/KL metrics and the 50-sample listening-study protocol. The objective-evaluation scenarios and Appendix A loudness sweep are also unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 3 retains the same component ablations. Figure 3's spectral comparisons, Appendix A's loudness sensitivity analysis and Appendix B's waveform-alignment examples are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both retain identical ± uncertainty reporting for OVL and PER in Table 2, without further defining those terms. No run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: All result entries and graphical findings are unchanged. For example, BNMusic retains direct-output EPIC-SOUNDS FAD/KL scores of 7.98/1.67 in Table 1 and OVL/PER scores of 3.67±0.55/3.84±0.63 in Table 2. Appendix results are identical.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, spectrogram and mask definitions, and Equations (1)–(5) are unchanged. No formal assumptions, mathematical reasoning or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims concerning personalized noise blending, noise-aligned music generation, adaptive amplification and improved auditory experience.

C2.justification: Interpretations of alignment, masking, ablations and the loudness–FAD relationship remain unchanged. Both retain the same limitations concerning prompt compatibility, conversion distortion, generation speed, listener fatigue and masking important environmental sounds.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures remain identical, including default Riffusion settings, α=0.14, Nvidia 4090 hardware, processing times and Appendix B's 10%–20% mask-selection guidance. The project-page link and resource-access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 removes Park et al.'s DiffSound work, previously reference 29, from Section 2.3 and the bibliography. Other reference changes concern metadata or numbering of the same works; the substantive research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Editorial revisions concentrate on bibliographic publication details, author/title formatting and removal of stray funding text from the watermarking reference title. The version/date stamp changes, while the body prose and section structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Bibliography edits cause limited reflow across pages 11–13, including reference 17 moving to page 12. Citation numbers change in Table 1's caption and headers, but figure designs, table structures and appendix layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: V3 adds bibliographic detail and cleans stray funding text from one reference title, but introduces malformed accent rendering in the FAD and Moûsai reference titles. These limited editorial changes leave the scientific evidence, reasoning, reproducibility information and main exposition unchanged, producing no meaningful net difference in overall quality.
